entries.0590c7d10bf56534: This is where a combination that looks surprising from the outside was born: a company making analytical instruments also makes aircraft equipment. It handles flight control systems, air management systems, cockpit display systems and engine accessories, and although its revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥43,371 million, the smallest of the 4 reportable segments, it grew 12.2% year on year, the largest growth rate, and segment profit of ¥8,220 million also grew the most, up 35.5% year on year. Against the small number of employees, 356 (with 26 temporary employees counted separately), the order backlog as of March 31, 2026 was ¥89,689 million, more than 2 times the revenue for the fiscal year, showing in the figures that this is a business that takes a long time to deliver.

entries.17d66f6eeb3ac78b: This business makes equipment for viewing the inside of the body in hospitals. It handles angiography systems, X-ray TV systems, general radiography systems, mobile ward-round systems that can be moved to patients' rooms, surgical X-ray TV systems used in operating rooms, PET systems, near-infrared optical camera systems, radiation therapy-related equipment and medical information systems. The business traces its origins to 1909, when Japan's first medical X-ray apparatus was completed. Manufacturing is carried out by Shimane Shimadzu Co., Ltd. and local subsidiaries in the United States, Germany and China, while domestic sales and maintenance services are handled by Shimadzu Medical Systems Corporation. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥73,794 million, the second largest by revenue, but segment profit of ¥4,871 million was the smallest of the four reportable segments, making this a business whose rankings differ greatly between revenue and profit. The number of employees was 1,982 (excluding 170 temporary employees). The company explains that revenue increased 1.7% year on year and operating profit increased 14.3% year on year, which is the second largest increase in profit growth rate after the Aircraft Equipment Business.

The company cites, as initiatives in the fiscal year, that it established a new base for its North America R&D Center in San Francisco and established new companies in India and Australia integrating the sales structures for analytical and medical products, and writes that it aims to build a development, production and sales structure based on local production for local consumption.

entries.48f6809998af0f26: In 1875, the first Genzo Shimadzu started, as a sole proprietorship, the business of manufacturing educational scientific instruments at Kiyamachi Nijo in Kyoto City. The securities report treats this as the company's founding. In September 1917, it was reorganized into a corporation with capital of ¥2 million, and Shimadzu Corporation was established (head office: Kiyamachi Nijo, Kyoto City). At the same time, it set up the Tokyo Branch (now a branch office), the Osaka Branch (now the Kansai Branch) and the Fukuoka Branch (now the Kyushu Branch). The head office moved in August 1919 to Kawaramachi Nijo, Nakagyo-ku, Kyoto City, and in December 1986 to the present Nishinokyo Kuwabara-cho, Nakagyo-ku, Kyoto City.

The company explains that revenue fell 1.1% year on year, the only decline among the four reportable segments, while operating profit rose 1.2% year on year. entries.e73c71da9af329e5: A business that makes instruments for examining what is contained in a substance and how much. The main products listed in the [[term:annual-securities-report|Annual Securities Report]] are chromatography systems that separate components of liquids and gases, mass spectrometry systems that identify substances by molecular weight, and various analysis systems using light, heat, X-rays and electron beams, as well as materials testing machines, fatigue and durability testing machines, non-destructive inspection systems, high-speed video cameras, balances and scales, and further clinical laboratory reagents and fully automated PCR testing systems. The makers and sellers are domestic subsidiaries such as Shimadzu Science Co., Ltd., Shimadzu Diagnostics Corporation and Shimadzu Rika Corporation, and local subsidiaries in the United States, Germany, the United Kingdom, China, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, the United Arab Emirates and Uruguay, while maintenance services are handled by Shimadzu Access Co., Ltd. Net sales to external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥364,908 million, accounting for 65% of the company's total net sales of ¥560,728 million, and segment profit of ¥52,578 million is also 2/3 or more of the ¥76,266 million total for the 4 reportable segments. The number of employees was 8,995 (excluding 660 temporary employees). Orders received were ¥366,517 million and the order backlog was ¥115,605 million. The company explains that net sales rose 4.9% and operating income rose 1.0% from the previous fiscal year.

entries.fd3917f3a8b484ee: A business that makes equipment installed on aircraft. It handles flight control systems that steer the aircraft, air management systems that maintain cabin air and temperature, cockpit display systems that show cockpit instruments, and engine accessories. The business began with the establishment of an aircraft equipment division in October 1956, and is carried out by Shimadzu Aerotech Co., Ltd. and Shimadzu Precision Instruments, Inc. (United States). Net sales to external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were ¥43,371 million, the smallest of the 4 reportable segments, but its 12.2% increase over the previous fiscal year was the highest growth rate, and segment profit of ¥8,220 million also grew the most, up 35.5%. The number of employees is 356 (excluding 26 temporary employees), also the fewest among the 4. The characteristic of this business is the length of time until delivery, and the order backlog at the end of the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥89,689 million, more than 2 times the same year's net sales of ¥43,371 million. Orders received in the period were ¥49,181 million, a 14.7% decrease from the previous fiscal year.
